Water Angels

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
South African's helping drought stricken communities by delivering water and food for starving farm animals.

Summary:
Interviewing Robbyn Wilkinson and Lisa Williams (in johannesburg - the Kayalami Equestrian community) who saw the drought devastation and decided to pack a horse cart and just start dropping off water, it grew and now have delivered food for the animals in the free state and water all over the free state.They have amazing video footage of people getting water.

Interview 2: Ray de Vries - (his partner is Caroline van Saasen - who George heard on 702) who began the initiative of holiday makers delivering water along their routes back to Johannesburg. Speak about social media aspect of this and show that we also put calls out.
ARTICLE:
Holidaymakers returning home please take water for people along the route.
This is the appeal made by Caroline van Saasen who took the initiative, only a few hours ago, to encourage holidaymakers who are on their way home to take water with them for communities en route. "I never expected in my wildest dreams that there would be such a response from fellow South Africans" said the mother of three from her new home in Mpumalanga. "My husband and I lost everything in the Free State and had to start again from scratch, so I just want to help other people by doing this. When we started this morning it was the communities that we knew in the Free State, but it is spreading fast throughout the country" she said. The group known as Water shortage South Africa / Waternood Suid Africa on Facebook has earmarked communities and is asking for volunteers to man them. At the time of writing George, Colesburg and Welkom already have drop-off zones manned by volunteers with offers coming in. Van Saasen is a mother of three children is a housewife and holds down a job as well. "I am just an average South African who wants to be part of the solution" said van Saasen. People are requested to please go to their Facebook page which is continually being updated.


Further information:
https://carp.co.za/sites/carp.co.za/files/suggestions/30091/water-deliveries-senekal.pdf


Fly to Bloemfontein - drive to smithfield.

Start day 2 in Smithfield going out with water trucks into townships and delivering water to communities - interview people there.
Come back to Bloem via Reddersburg - meet a group of farmers whose horses have been helped by Kayalami equestrian group.
Back to airport.

Press Release:


Water Angels
For many South Africans, the water crisis has reached rock bottom. But, while the country remains in the grip of a severe drought, relief has come from all corners. Social media awareness efforts have rallied schools, companies and private individuals to distribute water and animal feed to some of the Free State’s hardest hit areas in a desperate effort to save people and dying animals. Carte Blanche meets “average” South Africans whose tireless efforts are making a radical difference to those in need.


Script:


Video Audio
Pictures of the sun – dry arid terrain
MAP The heat from the arid land near Smithfield in the Free State sucks all moisture from the air as you breathe. (MAP)In this town, water isn’t a right. It’s a luxury.
LINK: I feel like I’m on the set of a mad max movie, water here is life, it’s called Metsi and the reality is that when it does come, it’s gone in a couple of minutes.”
Lerato: “You can’t wash, you can’t cook, you can’t do anything. Like myself, I’m unemployed and I survive by planting crops and sell to the local community. But I couldn’t do it this year.”
Lerato Qhomane supports eight thirsty people all living under her roof.
Lerato Qhomane, Smithfield resident Lerato: “It’s stressful, cos even if I didn’t want to, I have to save that water, because I don’t know whenI will get that other water again.”
Nearly 500km away, Middelburg resident and complete stranger, Caroline van Saasen, answered Lerato’s desperate plea for help.
Caroline: “I decided to just open a Facebook page, called water shortage south Africa and see if I can’t get the holidaymakers in south Africa to fill up 2litre water bottles and drop it off in towns and communities where there is a water need.”
Caroline van Saasen, Founder Water Shortage South Africa Caroline’s initiative exploded and in 16 days 1.2 million litre’s of water had been delivered to people like Lerato.

Water Shortage South Africa lit a viral fire of enthusiasm with water collection points appearing over night.
Caroline: “I’m just a plain housewife, I’ve got three teenage kids, one just past matric. I’m not a hero.”
Ray: “What the initiative did, was to get water into people’s mouths to drink.”
Ray de Vries woke up on New Years day and read about a farmer who committed suicide a day before the rain fell. This lead him to Caroline.
Ray: “Contacted the facebook site, I said ive got water in my car, where do you want me to go?
Went to Senekal, 72 people hadn’t showered or bathed for 28 days, these are frail care old age people. Nobody knew about them. 34.00 there was no island with a huge banner saying SOS help, but Facebook was.”
Devi link ”This is Reddersburg, 60 km south of Bloemfontein it didn’t rain in 2015, not a drop, but it’s become one of the many collection points across the free state.”
We met Joseph “Mafa” Madingiza, a farmer in Reddersburg who lost 11 of his 15 cattle the day before we arrived.
Joseph “Mafa” Madingiza Devi: “You lost 55 thousand rand?
Mafa: “Yes It’s a lot of money.
I feel very hurt, because I don’t know where I can get it again.”
Mafa says water has been delivered, but doesn’t know how much longer he can keep his remaining cattle alive.
Mafa: “I must always use petrol to go get water, and I only get a little bit of water, and it’s never enough for the cattle.”
Robbyn Wilkinson asked herself what about animals like Mafa’s cattle? After seeing Caroline’s Facebook page, she formed H2O for Hooves and Heels and began delivering water AND feed to communities in the Free State.
Robbyn Wilkinson,
H2O for Hooves and Heels Robbyn: “They were so excited from the kids to the chief, I made a mess up, I didn’t go and see the chief first, I didn’t understand the protocol.”
Devi: now you do.
Robbyn: Now I do.
Lisa Williams joined her, but stresses the need for the initiative to keep going.
Linda Williams
H2O for Hooves and Heels UPSOUND “I don’t know how long its going to take to replenish the grazing for the cattle, for the horses, for the donkey’s.”
Clara Carstens in Reddersburg was thrilled when H20 for Hooves and Heels made a special delivery.
Clara: “Extremely relieved and amazed, because I mean this initiative started last week. And they delivered 140 and it’s really nice feed.”
Clara feeds the animals in the nearby township and understands why they are thought of last.
Clara: “We can’t find food anymore, even the people who can still buy food can’t find food.”
Clara found this horse too late, but hopes to save these from a similar fate.
Ian Rudolph, DA councilor
In nearby Smithfield, Ian Rudolph is called Mr. Water. He owns a guesthouse with a borehole. With help from Joseph Masoli, they transport the bottles sent by initiatives like Water Shortage South Africa to the people. The smiling faces cover the trauma of their present reality.
Joseph: “Some of the people have lost their children, so they are struggling, especially old mothers and grandfathers. So, we are so very happy to help these people with water.”
Devi: “When was the last time people were this excited to see you, even in your own families?” (laugh)
BABY PIC With buckets ready, mothers and their babies wait anxiously, hoping the water doesn’t run out before it’s their turn. But, gogo Lerato says rather than despair, she’s grateful and remains hopeful that the rain will come soon.
5.20 “We have to save water, so we’ll have to change our lifestyle.”



PROMOS:
10 seconder:
In the drought-stricken Free State, water isn’t a right. It’s a luxury. But help is on the way from initiatives around the country.
15 Seconder1:
South Africans are pulling together to donate water to desperate people surviving daily in the grip of the Free State drought.
Ray: “What the initiative did, was to get water into people’s mouths to drink.”
Lerato: “We have to save water, so we’ll have to change our lifestyle.”
15 Seconder2:
For desperate South Africans living in the drought-stricken Free State, water shortages are at their worst.
Lerato: “I need to save this water, because I don’t know when it will come again.”
But relief is on the way.
